rationale: Recorded the reproduction of the partition experiment: the repeat execution of the same fixed inputs (receipt f116b7a68ef049ba83d7a9d4f6b8a07e, exit 0, test passed, 51 events) reproduced every comparison outcome of the original receipt 91832b58570e4cc7842cfff4d04836e0 at the same parsed indices — both sides leading and both holding the same term, no cross-side entry, and a single leader in the flag-disabled control — so the account's strongest consequence now rests on two independent executions of the same fixed inputs. The split-brain fact cites both receipts, the interpretation notes explicitly that this establishes reproducibility under the declared conditions rather than schedule independence, and nothing else changes.

knowledge.statement: In the retained partition execution the reconstruction produced two leaders in the same term with disjoint quorums: the restarted node led on its single-voter reconstruction while the two peers it was partitioned from led on the committed three-voter configuration, both sides committed a uniquely named entry (both apply calls returned success), the first side's configuration named one voter against the second side's three, and neither side's log store contained the other side's entry (cross_entries_seen 0), so the cluster held two committed histories. With the flag disabled the same partition left the restarted node unable to lead with only one of the committed configuration's three voters reachable and produced a single leader.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter committed configuration recorded at log index 106 while the restarted node's snapshot metadata carries a single-voter configuration; the node is disconnected from the other two in both directions with the transport's Disconnect and then stopped and restarted with a fresh empty instance beside it, and the other two keep the committed configuration; the two sides are given up to 800 ms to elect and 1500 ms to commit, and the partition is never healed in the execution. Reproduced by a repeat execution of the same fixed inputs at the same parsed indices.

investigations.discriminator: Every consequence this account identified is exercised, and the strongest one (two leaders in the same term under a partition) has now been reproduced by a repeat of the same fixed inputs. What remains outside is only the surrounding fault and storage model: a disk-backed commit-tracking store, crash and restart timing, a healed partition, and further repetitions or longer runs. Those are recorded as limitations rather than as open questions.

interpretations.rationale: Two independent executions of the same fixed partition experiment now agree. Receipt 91832b58570e4cc7842cfff4d04836e0 executed it first, and the repeat receipt f116b7a68ef049ba83d7a9d4f6b8a07e (exit 0, test passed, 51 parsed events, run from the retained fixed inputs rather than from the current draft) reproduced every outcome at the same parsed indices: comparisons 0, 1 and 2 violated with one valid witness at parsed index 48 (both sides leading, both leaders in the same term, and cross_entries_seen 0) and comparison 3 holding at parsed index 50 for the flag-disabled control. The current account therefore stands with the strongest consequence reproducible under the declared conditions: the startup reconstruction diverges from the node's own log because the configuration scan starts above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied) after restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied to the tracked commit index [scan_start, restore_lastapplied, cfg_entry]; that context persists under a live healthy leader until a configuration entry is appended; and it then produces bounded non-progress, leadership and commits resting on a minority of the committed configuration, a client-acknowledged commit that rests on one copy or is discarded entirely, votes and leadership granted without entitlement, a client membership change that replaces the committed configuration with support that is not its majority, and — when a partition separates the two configurations — two leaders in the same term whose committed histories never meet. What the repeat adds is reproducibility of the exercised schedule and conditions, not independence from them, and not a rate or a long-run property; the remaining boundaries are the ones listed below.
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, produces these effects: excluded wherever tested, by the within-flag case whose configuration entry lies above the replayed prefix and by the flag-disabled controls in every receipt, which hold the published configuration and refuse the same requests, decisions, changes and leadership.

Each consequence needs its stated conditions: the partition case needs the two sides physically separated and the restarted side to reach a quorum of its own reconstruction; the discard needs the successor leadership to outrank the stale holder's term; the campaign needed the former leader down; the client change needs prevIndex 0 and the committed configuration's voters unreachable. These are the conditions under which the consequences hold, not unconditional effects.

The two partition receipts share the same inputs, the same process model and the same schedule; they establish that the outcome repeats under those declared conditions, not that it is independent of them.
limitations: Single process with in-memory transports and in-memory commit-tracking stores, no crash injection, no disk-backed store and no network fault model beyond the transport's own Disconnect.

Single-shot windows (200-1500 ms depending on the case, 3000 ms for leadership, 1000-1500 ms for commits) and one or two restarted instances per case; the partition outcome is reproduced twice but no rate, longer-run or long-stability claim follows.
The partition is never healed and no client is served across the healed state, so convergence after healing, membership reconciliation and any data reconciliation are unexercised.

The reconstruction shapes beyond the five exercised ladders, other stores and other configuration flags were not varied; the LogCache entries record a separate startup-plumbing gap rather than a consensus consequence.
